title: Pelagos Global Port & Canal Disbursement Intelligence Discovery Inventory
author: Pelagos Core Intelligence & Optimization Team

sources.source_name: Panama Canal Official Maritime Tariffs & Tolls Schedule
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download official tariff schedule PDF and periodic OP Notices to Shipping (N-1, N-7)
sources.access_restrictions: Publicly accessible online tariff schedules; interactive VUMPA pre-arrival filing portal requires agent credentials for formal transit booking
sources.update_frequency: Annual baseline tariff updates with ad-hoc OP Notices for draught/freshwater surcharges
sources.historical_coverage: Comprehensive historical circulars and tariff schedules from 2016 Neopanamax expansion to present
sources.calculation_methodology: Two-tier toll system (fixed capacity charge + variable PC/UMS tonnage toll) plus variable Freshwater Surcharge (FWS: fixed component 1-2% + variable dynamic component 0-10% based on Gatun Lake water level) plus transit reservation auction/slot fees plus mandatory ACP tug and pilotage assignments based on LOA/beam
sources.known_gaps: VUMPA live booking auction prices fluctuate dynamically and cannot be determined purely from static published tariffs; draft adjustments announced bi-weekly based on hydrologic forecasts
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Periodic manual PDF/circular ingestion of ACP OP Notices with structured rule encoding; live Gatun water level parameterization

sources.source_name: Suez Canal Navigation Circulars, Toll Schedules & Marketing Policies
sources.port_canal_coverage: Suez Canal (Port Said EGPSD / Port Tewfik EGSUE)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual navigation circulars and periodical surcharge notifications as PDF
sources.access_restrictions: Publicly accessible online tariff portal and periodical circulars; rebate applications require prior agent submission
sources.update_frequency: Annual base circular with frequent quarterly/monthly periodical surcharge amendments
sources.historical_coverage: Navigation circulars archived from 2000 to present
sources.calculation_methodology: Tolls denominated in IMF Special Drawing Rights (SDR), calculated progressively across SCNT tiers, differentiated by vessel type (Bulk Carrier, Tanker, Container) and loading condition (Laden vs Ballast), multiplied by active periodical surcharge circular percentage (e.g. 5% to 15% surcharge), plus mandatory Suez Canal pilotage, escort tugs (compulsory based on SCNT/DWT/beam), projector rental and mooring boat fees
sources.known_gaps: Settlement converted from SDR to hard currency (USD, EUR) at National Bank of Egypt daily exchange rate; long-haul circular rebates require formal application before voyage commencement and cannot be guaranteed ex-ante
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Semi-automated monitoring of SCA Navigation Circulars; rule-based SDR toll calculation engine with explicit currency cross-rate conversion

sources.source_name: Kiel Canal Transit Fee Ordinance (NOKBefAbgV) & Pilotage Regulations
sources.country_and_geographic_coverage: Germany / Northern Europe (North Sea - Baltic Sea Corridor)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download ordinance text and statutory annex fee tables (Anlage 1) from ELWIS
sources.access_restrictions: Public legal gazette, open access
sources.update_frequency: Periodic legislative amendments (e.g. 50% transit fee reduction decree under § 8)
sources.historical_coverage: Complete statutory history in Federal Law Gazette
sources.calculation_methodology: Stepwise bracket formula based on Gross Tonnage (GT) and Traffic Group (Verkehrsgruppe 1 to 6 determined by length, beam, and draft); total transit cost consists of three statutory pillars: (1) Canal Dues (Kanalabgaben), (2) Pilot Dues (Lotsabgaben - infrastructure), and (3) Pilot Fees (Lotsgelder - service) plus Canal Helmsmen (Kanallotse/Steuerleute) where compulsory
sources.known_gaps: Temporary fee reductions (e.g. 50% discount under § 8) extended annually by ministerial decree; must be tracked for expiration
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Direct statutory parameter ingestion from ELWIS legal annex tables into static configuration tables

sources.source_name: St. Lawrence Seaway Schedule of Tolls
sources.publishing_organization: St. Lawrence Seaway Management Corp (SLSMC) / Great Lakes St. Lawrence Seaway Development Corp (GLS)
sources.country_and_geographic_coverage: Canada & United States / Great Lakes - St. Lawrence System
sources.available_data_format: PDF, HTML, US Federal Register publication
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual Schedule of Tolls PDF from greatlakes-seaway.com
sources.access_restrictions: Public access under bilateral US-Canada treaty framework
sources.update_frequency: Annual (published prior to season opening in March)
sources.historical_coverage: Annual schedules preserved from 1959 to present
sources.calculation_methodology: Two-component composite toll: (1) Charge per Gross Registered Ton of vessel, plus (2) Charge per metric ton of cargo (differentiated by bulk, grain, general, steel), assessed separately for MLO section and Welland Canal. Split currency invoicing (Canadian dollars for SLSMC locks, US dollars for GLS locks)
sources.known_gaps: Lockage delays and winter surcharge operational windows require real-time navigation notice tracking
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Annual PDF harvest and table extraction into structured rule model

sources.source_name: MPA Port Dues Tariff & Green Port Programme Circulars
sources.publishing_organization: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download Port Dues Tariff circular and Port Regulations from mpa.gov.sg
sources.access_restrictions: Public statutory tariff schedule
sources.update_frequency: Periodic multi-year reviews via Port Marine Circulars
sources.historical_coverage: Published schedules maintained online with circular archives
sources.calculation_methodology: Rate per 100 Gross Tonnage (GT) or part thereof, scaled by purpose of call (loading/discharging cargo, bunkering only, ship repair, taking supplies) and length of stay (24-hour periods up to 30 days, 6-month, and annual schemes). Discounted rate (e.g. 50% concession) for pure bunker calls <= 24 hours. Green Port Programme provides 25-30% reduction for LNG/low-carbon fuels
sources.known_gaps: Does not cover pilotage, towage, or berthage, which are operated commercially by PSA Marine and terminal operators
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Manual ingestion of statutory circular tariff tables into relational rule schema

sources.source_name: PSA Marine Pilotage & Towage Tariff Schedule
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download public tariff revision circulars; full tariff card requires IMOS customer credentials
sources.access_restrictions: Public summary circulars available; live fuel BAF and full itemized schedule restricted to IMOS portal users
sources.update_frequency: Annual pilotage adjustments; monthly/quarterly Towage Bunker Adjustment Factor updates
sources.historical_coverage: Recent circulars publicly visible (2022-2024)
sources.calculation_methodology: Pilotage billed per vessel Gross Tonnage bracket per hour (e.g. <=6000 GT: SGD 236/hr, 6001-12000 GT: SGD 261.50/hr, scaling upwards). Towage billed per tug per hour based on bollard pull capacity, plus dynamic Towage Bunker Adjustment Factor
sources.known_gaps: Dynamic monthly Towage BAF requires customer login; exact tug count required is determined by MPA Harbour Craft Regulations / Pilot discretion rather than deterministic tariff rule
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Store public baseline circular tiers in research registry; flag monthly BAF as UNVERIFIED without customer login

sources.source_name: General Terms and Conditions including Seaport Dues
sources.publishing_organization: Port of Rotterdam Authority (Havenbedrijf Rotterdam N.V.)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual 'General Terms and Conditions including Port Tariffs' PDF
sources.access_restrictions: Public document download; digital declaration requires IAMConnected registration
sources.update_frequency: Annual (effective 1 January)
sources.historical_coverage: Complete tariff booklets preserved from 2010 to present
sources.calculation_methodology: Two-part composite formula: Seaport Dues = (Tonnage Component: GT * Rate_GT) + (Cargo Component: Tonnes * Rate_Cargo), subject to category-specific minimum and maximum caps. Additional fixed charges for compulsory ship waste reception (SAB). Discounts granted for high Environmental Ship Index (ESI >= 31) and Green Award
sources.known_gaps: Does not include pilotage (Loodswezen) or commercial towage/mooring (Boluda/Kotug/KRVE)
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Annual PDF harvest and table parsing into normalized PortTariff and PortChargeRule entities

sources.source_name: Regulated Dutch Maritime Pilotage Tariffs & ACM Orders
sources.publishing_organization: Nederlands Loodswezen B.V. / Autoriteit Consument & Markt (ACM)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual ACM tariff determination decree and Loodswezen regional tariff booklets
sources.access_restrictions: Publicly accessible online tariff schedules and interactive calculator
sources.update_frequency: Annual (regulated by ACM decree under Pilotage Act / Loodsenwet)
sources.historical_coverage: Regulated tariff schedules available for 10+ years
sources.calculation_methodology: Statutory three-factor formula: Total Pilotage = S (fixed start rate) + T (vessel size factor based on Gross Tonnage and draught in decimeters) + A (navigational channel / approach distance factor). Surcharges for ordering within short notice (<4 hours) or cancellation
sources.known_gaps: Does not include pilot boat helicopter delivery surcharge when extreme weather bars conventional launch
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest annual ACM statutory formula constants into rule tables

sources.source_name: Port of Antwerp-Bruges Tariff Regulations for Sea-Going Vessels
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual Tariff Regulations booklet from portofantwerpbruges.com
sources.access_restrictions: Public access
sources.update_frequency: Annual CPI indexation (effective 1 January)
sources.historical_coverage: Preserved tariff schedules from pre-merger Antwerp/Zeebrugge through unified authority
sources.calculation_methodology: Tonnage Dues (based on vessel GT and stay duration, granting first 30 days of stay) + Mooring Rights (based on volume/weight of cargo handled). ESI discounts of 10% to 15% applied to tonnage dues for qualifying vessels
sources.known_gaps: River Scheldt pilotage administered separately by Flemish Agency for Maritime Services and Coast (MDK); lock pilotage and boatmen handled by Brabo
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Annual PDF harvest and table extraction into PortTariff schema

sources.source_name: Port of Houston Authority Tariff No. 8 & Terminal Schedules
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download published Tariff No. 8 PDF from porthouston.com
sources.access_restrictions: Public access pursuant to US Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) regulations
sources.update_frequency: Annual revisions with periodic FMC item amendments
sources.historical_coverage: Tariff books and past amendments filed with FMC
sources.calculation_methodology: Dockage calculated per foot of Length Overall (LOA) per 24-hour period or fraction thereof, using progressive length brackets. Harbour Fee assessed per vessel call based on LOA. Wharfage assessed on cargo loaded/unloaded per short ton (2,000 lbs). Port Security Surcharge added as percentage of dockage
sources.known_gaps: Does not include Houston Pilots charges or commercial ship-assist tugs (e.g. Moran, Kirby, Suderman & Young)
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingestion of FMC-filed Tariff No. 8 rate tables; LOA unit conversion from feet to meters

sources.source_name: Houston Pilots Official Tariff Schedule
sources.publishing_organization: Houston Pilots Association / Board of Pilot Commissioners for Harris County Ports
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download published Houston Pilots Tariff PDF from houston-pilots.com or Harris County Pilot Board
sources.access_restrictions: Public access under Texas State Transportation Code Title 4 Chapter 66
sources.update_frequency: Annual or bi-annual rate orders approved by Pilot Board
sources.historical_coverage: Pilot board rate orders archived on public record
sources.calculation_methodology: Bipartite statutory formula: Total Pilotage = (Draft Charge: Draft in feet * Zone Draft Rate) + (Unit Charge: Vessel Units * Zone Unit Rate) + Communications/Transport Fee. Vessel Units = (LOA in feet * Extreme Breadth in feet) / 100. Minimum draft 24 feet enforced for vessels >= 450 feet LOA. Surcharges for drafts > 40 feet
sources.known_gaps: Docking pilot services at private terminals may be distinct from channel transit pilots
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Deterministic rule encoding of Houston Pilots formula into PilotageRule entity

sources.source_name: Oregon Board of Maritime Pilots Rate Orders & Tariffs
sources.publishing_organization: Oregon Board of Maritime Pilots (OBMP) / State of Oregon
sources.port_canal_coverage: Columbia & Willamette Rivers (USPDX, USKAL, USLWW, USVAN)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download published OBMP Board Rate Orders from oregon.gov
sources.access_restrictions: Public access under Oregon Revised Statutes (ORS 776)
sources.update_frequency: Annual or bi-annual contested case rate determinations
sources.historical_coverage: State administrative orders archived from 1990s to present
sources.calculation_methodology: Separate Bar crossing and River transit tariffs: (1) Columbia River Bar Pilots: Draft fee ($/ft) + Tonnage fee ($/GT) + Pilot boat surcharge. (2) Columbia River Pilots: Draft fee ($/ft) + Tonnage fee ($/GT) + Mileage zone fee based on river mile destination (Astoria, Longview, Kalama, Portland)
sources.known_gaps: Vessel transit requiring both Bar and River grounds pays two distinct pilotage fees
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Encode OBMP rate orders into two-stage pilotage model for Columbia River corridor

sources.source_name: US Harbor Maintenance Fee (HMF) Statutory Regulations
sources.publishing_organization: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) / U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP)
sources.country_and_geographic_coverage: United States (Federal / All US Commercial Seaports)
sources.port_canal_coverage: All federally maintained commercial navigation channels in US
sources.available_data_format: HTML, Code of Federal Regulations (19 CFR § 24.24), US Code (19 U.S.C. § 4461)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Statutory legal text inspection
sources.access_restrictions: Public domain US Federal Law
sources.update_frequency: Statutory rate fixed by Congress (Water Resources Development Act)
sources.historical_coverage: Established in 1986 WRDA
sources.calculation_methodology: Ad valorem assessment of 0.125% (0.00125) of the value of commercial cargo loaded or unloaded at federally maintained ports. Assessed primarily on imports and domestic shipments (export HMF held unconstitutional under US Supreme Court US v. Shoe Corp)
sources.known_gaps: Does not apply to pure vessel movements without cargo; export bulk cargoes are exempt
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Static parameter rule (0.125% ad valorem) tagged to import cargo valuations

sources.source_name: Vancouver Fraser Port Authority Fee Document
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual Port Authority Fee Document PDF from portvancouver.com
sources.access_restrictions: Public notice pursuant to Canada Marine Act Section 49
sources.update_frequency: Annual (published 60 days prior to 1 January effective date)
sources.historical_coverage: Annual fee documents preserved on port archive
sources.calculation_methodology: Harbour Dues assessed per GRT for first 5 calls in a calendar year (subsequent calls exempt). Berthage assessed per meter of LOA per hour of berth occupancy. Wharfage assessed per metric ton of cargo handled. EcoAction provides 23% to 47% harbour dues discounts for clean vessels
sources.known_gaps: Does not include Pacific Pilotage Authority charges or commercial tugboat services (Seaspan / SAAM)
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Annual PDF harvest and table extraction into PortTariff schema

sources.source_name: Pacific Pilotage Authority Customer Guide to Pilotage Charges
sources.port_canal_coverage: British Columbia Coastal Waters (Vancouver, Roberts Bank, Prince Rupert)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download Customer Guide to Charges PDF from ppa.gc.ca
sources.access_restrictions: Public regulations issued under Canada Pilotage Act
sources.update_frequency: Annual or periodic service charge adjustments
sources.historical_coverage: Archived customer guides and regulatory amendments
sources.calculation_methodology: Two-factor formula: Vessel Units = (LOA * Beam) / 100 multiplied by Unit Rate, plus Hourly Time Charge for transit duration, plus boarding fee (pilot boat launch at Victoria/Brotchie Ledge or helicopter)
sources.known_gaps: Dynamic fuel surcharge on pilot boats adjusted quarterly based on local marine diesel prices
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest PPA formula and baseline unit rates into PilotageRule entity

sources.source_name: Port of London Authority Charges Terms and Conditions
sources.available_data_format: PDF, HTML, Online Visit Charges Estimator
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual Rates & Charges booklet from pla.co.uk
sources.access_restrictions: Public access under Port of London Act 1968
sources.update_frequency: Annual (effective 1 January)
sources.historical_coverage: Preserved tariff schedules available online
sources.calculation_methodology: Vessel Conservancy Charge assessed on GT per entry. Cargo Conservancy Charge assessed per metric ton of cargo loaded/discharged. Pilotage calculated on draught and distance zones along Thames. ESI discounts of up to 25% for high-scoring vessels
sources.known_gaps: Terminal handling and stevedoring at private terminals (e.g. London Gateway, Tilbury) are separate commercial agreements
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Harvest annual PLA schedule and test against online Visit Charges Estimator

sources.source_name: General Lighthouse Authorities Statutory Light Dues Regulations
sources.port_canal_coverage: All UK and Irish commercial ports
sources.available_data_format: HTML, Statutory Instruments (UK SI), DfT Guidance
sources.manual_download_requirements: Inspect statutory instrument and Trinity House guidance page
sources.access_restrictions: Open UK Government Legislation
sources.update_frequency: Annual statutory review (effective 1 April)
sources.historical_coverage: Statutory Instruments preserved on legislation.gov.uk
sources.calculation_methodology: Levied at statutory rate (46 pence per NRT effective April 2026) on Net Registered Tonnage, capped at 50,000 NRT per call. Maximum 9 chargeable voyages per vessel per year in UK/Irish waters. 1-month exemption from further light dues after initial call
sources.known_gaps: Tonnage deck cargo rules apply to container and timber vessels
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Direct statutory parameter rule in Pelagos disbursement engine

sources.source_name: Puertos del Estado / Valenciaport Tasas Portuarias Schedule
sources.publishing_organization: Autoridad Portuaria de Valencia (APV) / Puertos del Estado
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual Tasas Portuarias circular from valenciaport.com and Ley de Puertos (TRLPEMM)
sources.access_restrictions: Public access under Spanish administrative law (Real Decreto Legislativo 2/2011)
sources.update_frequency: Annual State Budget Law updates and Port Authority board resolutions
sources.historical_coverage: Published in official state gazette (BOE)
sources.calculation_methodology: Standard Spanish statutory formula: T-1 (Vessel Tax) = Basic Amount * Corrective Coefficient * (GT / 100) * Time periods in port, differentiated by Zone I (interior waters) and Zone II (exterior waters). T-3 (Cargo Tax) = Basic Amount * Coefficient * Tonnes * Cargo Group. Environmental discounts under Article 245 of TRLPEMM
sources.known_gaps: Towage and mooring services provided by private licensees (Boluda Towage, Prácticos de Valencia) with separate tariffs
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest national TRLPEMM formula combined with Valenciaport local corrective coefficients

sources.source_name: JNPA Scale of Rates & Online Tariff Calculator
sources.available_data_format: PDF Gazette, Online Interactive Tariff Calculator
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download official Gazette notification Scale of Rates PDF from jnport.gov.in
sources.access_restrictions: Public statutory tariff schedule approved under Major Port Authorities Act 2021
sources.update_frequency: Annual or periodic revision under Major Port Adjudicatory Board orders
sources.historical_coverage: Gazette notifications preserved from 1990s through TAMP archives
sources.calculation_methodology: Statutory Scale of Rates: (1) Port Dues assessed on GT per entry (differentiated between foreign run in USD and coastal run in INR). (2) Pilotage-cum-Towage: composite charge based on GT covering one inward and one outward movement including pilot and tugs. (3) Berth Hire: charged per GT per hour or fraction thereof alongside. Settlement of foreign vessel charges in USD or INR at SBI TT buying rate
sources.known_gaps: Terminal handling charges (THC) at privatized container terminals (BMCT, APMT, NSICT) governed by separate concessionaire SORs
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest Gazette Scale of Rates table into PortTariff schema; benchmark against JNPA online calculator

sources.source_name: Deendayal Port Authority Scale of Rates (VRC & CRC)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download Scale of Rates PDF chapters from deendayalport.gov.in
sources.access_restrictions: Public statutory tariff schedule approved under Major Port Authorities Act 2021
sources.update_frequency: Annual escalations indexed to wholesale price movements
sources.historical_coverage: Comprehensive tariff chapters and TAMP orders online
sources.calculation_methodology: Chapter II Vessel-Related Charges (VRC): Port dues levied per GT per entry valid for 30 days. Pilotage fee per GT covering inward/outward pilotage and authorized tug assistance. Berth hire per GT per hour for dry cargo berths and oil jetties
sources.known_gaps: Tug assistance beyond standard allowance charged at additional hourly tug rates
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest DPA Gazette chapters into PortTariff and PortChargeRule tables

sources.source_name: Adani Ports Berthing Policy and Tariff Structure (BPTS)
sources.publishing_organization: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited (APSEZ)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual BPTS booklet PDF from adaniports.com
sources.access_restrictions: Publicly downloadable operational tariff booklet
sources.update_frequency: Annual booklet update (effective 1 April or 1 October)
sources.historical_coverage: Periodic BPTS booklets published on corporate site
sources.calculation_methodology: Private port commercial tariff: Port Dues per GT + Composite Pilotage & Towage charge per GT (with minimum dollar floor) + Fuel Surcharge per GT on pilotage movements + Berth Hire per GT per day. Strict operational penal charges for vessel non-readiness or failure to vacate berth within 2 hours
sources.known_gaps: Berthing priority fees (Cold Move / Priority Berthing) subject to bilateral commercial negotiation
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest APSEZ BPTS booklet rules into PortTariff schema

sources.source_name: Port of Yokohama Public Marine Terminal Tariffs & Municipal Dues
sources.publishing_organization: Port and Harbor Bureau, City of Yokohama
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download City of Yokohama port ordinance and public terminal tariff schedules
sources.access_restrictions: Public municipal gazette and port bureau regulations
sources.update_frequency: Periodic municipal ordinance revisions
sources.historical_coverage: Municipal gazette records archived
sources.calculation_methodology: Two-tier framework: (1) Municipal Port Entry Dues (Nyuko-ryo) assessed per GT upon entering port limits. (2) Public Berthage/Wharfage (Keiryu-ryo) assessed per GT per 24 hours of berthing occupancy. Note: Federal Tonnage Tax and Special Tonnage Tax assessed separately by Japan Customs under national law
sources.known_gaps: Tokyo Bay pilotage and harbor tugs (e.g. Tokyo Kisen, Wing Maritime) operated under private/association tariffs not covered by municipal bureau
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest municipal ordinance rates and link to national Japan Tonnage Tax schedule

sources.source_name: Japan Pilotage Tariff Formula (Pilotage Law Enforcement Regulations)
sources.publishing_organization: Japan Federation of Pilots' Associations (JFPA) / Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT)
sources.port_canal_coverage: Tokyo Bay (Yokohama/Chiba/Tokyo), Osaka Bay, Ise Bay, Inland Sea
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download JFPA pilotage fee schedule and MLIT Pilotage Law Enforcement Regulations
sources.access_restrictions: Public statutory tariff schedule approved by MLIT Minister
sources.update_frequency: Periodic review approved by MLIT
sources.historical_coverage: Statutory formulas preserved under Pilotage Law
sources.calculation_methodology: Standard national pilotage formula: Fee = A * [1 + 0.1 * (GRT - 1,000) / 1,000] * [1 + 0.1 * (D - 3.0) / 0.3], where A is the route basic rate, GRT is gross tonnage (fractions rounded up), and D is deepest draft in meters. Surcharges: 50% night work, bad weather addition
sources.known_gaps: Compulsory pilotage thresholds vary by district (e.g. >= 10,000 GT in Tokyo Bay vs >= 3,000 GT for specific hazardous carriers)
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Deterministic Python implementation of JFPA formula in PilotageRule entity

sources.source_name: China Port Charges Management Rules (港口收费计费办法)
sources.publishing_organization: Ministry of Transport (MOT) & National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC)
sources.port_canal_coverage: All Chinese coastal and inland ports (Shanghai CNSHA, Ningbo-Zhoushan, Shenzhen, Tianjin, Qingdao)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download MOT/NDRC circulars and individual port group tariff lists (收费目录清单)
sources.access_restrictions: Public regulatory decree of State Council ministries
sources.update_frequency: Periodic national logistics cost optimization circulars (e.g. 2017, 2019, 2022 reforms)
sources.historical_coverage: Full regulatory evolution since market reform archived on MOT portal
sources.calculation_methodology: Three-tier pricing framework: (1) Government-Fixed: Cargo port dues, security fees. (2) Government-Guided benchmark caps: Pilotage assessed on Net Tonnage (NT) and distance zones; Towage assessed on tug engine horsepower and hours utilized; Berthing dues assessed on NT per day. (3) Market-Regulated: Stevedoring and ancillary services. Strict mandatory public disclosure via Tariff Directory List
sources.known_gaps: Currency exchange settlement into foreign currencies and agency disbursement margins require port agent verification
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest national benchmark guide caps and cross-reference with SIPG (Shanghai) published tariff directory

sources.source_name: DP World UAE Region Port Tariff Book (Jebel Ali Port & Mina Rashid)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download DP World UAE Region Tariff Book PDF from dpworld.com
sources.access_restrictions: Publicly downloadable tariff booklet
sources.update_frequency: Periodic multi-year reviews with published addenda
sources.historical_coverage: Current and previous tariff books available on maritime archives
sources.calculation_methodology: Port Dues assessed on vessel GRT per entry for specified duration. Pilotage charged per movement using progressive GRT brackets. Towage charged per tug per movement based on vessel GRT. Berth occupancy charged per GRT per day after initial period
sources.known_gaps: Dangerous cargo (IMDG) surcharges and special environmental clearance fees require agent manifest submission
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest DP World tariff schedule into PortTariff schema; AED to USD currency conversion

sources.source_name: Pilbara Ports Authority Schedule of Port Charges
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual Schedule of Port Charges PDF from pilbaraports.com.au
sources.access_restrictions: Public access under Western Australia Port Authorities Act 1999
sources.update_frequency: Annual (effective 1 July Australian fiscal year)
sources.historical_coverage: Annual schedules preserved from 2014 merger to present
sources.calculation_methodology: Statutory Schedule under Port Authorities Act: Port Dues assessed per GT (providing 24-hr access). Pilotage mandatory for all commercial bulk carriers, billed per movement based on vessel GT. Berthage assessed per GT per hour alongside iron ore/salt berths
sources.known_gaps: Escort towage at Port Hedland operated under long-term licensee contracts (e.g. Svitzer/BHP tug fleet) with specialized cape-size escort tariff
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest PPA schedule into PortTariff schema; AUD to USD conversion

sources.source_name: Port of Melbourne Reference Tariff Schedule (RTS)
sources.publishing_organization: Port of Melbourne Operations Pty Ltd / Essential Services Commission (ESC)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual Reference Tariff Schedule PDF from portofmelbourne.com
sources.access_restrictions: Regulated under Victorian Pricing Order and Port Management Act 1995
sources.update_frequency: Annual (effective 1 July)
sources.historical_coverage: Regulated RTS archives maintained online under ESC oversight
sources.calculation_methodology: Prescribed service charges: Channel Fee assessed on vessel GT per call for access to Port Phillip channels. Berth Hire assessed per hour of occupancy at public berths. Wharfage assessed per metric ton or CBM of cargo handled
sources.known_gaps: Does not include Port Phillip Sea Pilots charges or commercial towage (Svitzer/Tug Services)
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest RTS schedule into PortTariff schema; AUD to USD conversion

sources.source_name: Porto de Santos Tabela de Tarifas Portuárias (ANTAQ)
sources.available_data_format: PDF, HTML, ANTAQ Painel de Administração Portuária
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download Tabela de Tarifas booklet from portodesantos.com.br or ANTAQ portal
sources.access_restrictions: Public access under Brazilian federal regulatory framework (ANTAQ)
sources.update_frequency: Annual or ordinary/extraordinary ANTAQ tariff review resolutions
sources.historical_coverage: Standardized Brazilian port tariff tables preserved on ANTAQ dashboard
sources.calculation_methodology: Standardized Brazilian structure: Tabela I (Acesso Aquaviário) assessed on DWT or cargo volume for waterway dredging and navigation access. Tabela II (Acostagem) assessed per linear meter of LOA per day alongside public quay. Pilotage (Praticagem de Santos) is private compulsory service regulated separately under Marinha do Brasil directives
sources.known_gaps: Pilotage fees in Brazil are subject to frequent private pricing disputes and lack unified public formula tables
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest APS Tabela I and II rules; BRL to USD exchange rate tracking

sources.source_name: Transnet National Ports Authority Port Tariff Book
sources.publishing_organization: Transnet National Ports Authority (TNPA) / Ports Regulator of South Africa (PRSA)
sources.port_canal_coverage: Durban (ZADUR), Richards Bay (ZARCB), Cape Town (ZACPT), Saldanha (ZASLD)
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download annual Port Tariff Book PDF from transnet.net or portsregulator.org
sources.access_restrictions: Public statutory tariff schedule approved under South Africa National Ports Act 2005
sources.update_frequency: Annual (effective 1 April following PRSA tariff determination)
sources.historical_coverage: Annual tariff books and PRSA determination directives preserved
sources.calculation_methodology: Unified national tariff across all 8 commercial ports: Port Dues assessed per 100 GRT for 24-hr period. Pilotage compulsory, calculated as Base Fee + Increment per 100 GRT (50% surcharge outside normal hours). Towage assessed per tug based on vessel GRT bracket. Berth dues assessed per 100 GRT per hour
sources.known_gaps: Overtime pilotage and tug cancellation penalties represent significant operational variability in South African ports
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Ingest unified TNPA Tariff Book rules into PortTariff schema; ZAR to USD conversion

sources.source_name: UNCTAD Port Pricing & Performance Indicator Framework
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download UNCTAD TrainForTrade manuals and RMT flagship reports
sources.access_restrictions: Open UN documentation and statistics
sources.update_frequency: Annual Review of Maritime Transport
sources.historical_coverage: Long-term historical maritime trade series (1968-present)
sources.calculation_methodology: Standard global taxonomy distinguishing: (1) Port Dues (general use of port infrastructure without pointing to specific measurable service), (2) Specific Port Tariffs (explicit service charges like pilotage/towage), and (3) Property/Concession Fees
sources.known_gaps: UNCTAD provides macroeconomic and regulatory frameworks, not port-specific line-item rate cards
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Adopt UNCTAD taxonomy for canonical disbursement schema design

sources.source_name: FONASBA Standard Port Agency Conditions & Proforma Disbursement Framework
sources.publishing_organization: Federation of National Associations of Ship Brokers and Agents (FONASBA) / BIMCO
sources.manual_download_requirements: Download FONASBA Standard Conditions and BIMCO agency templates
sources.access_restrictions: Public standard guidelines and contract forms
sources.update_frequency: Periodic multi-year standard updates
sources.historical_coverage: Standard conditions established in 1990s
sources.calculation_methodology: Defines standard contractual separation between statutory authority dues, third-party provider costs, and agent remuneration (Normal Agency Fee + communication/transport out-of-pocket expenses + additional fee per day for extended port stays beyond standard window)
sources.known_gaps: Agency fee amounts are commercially agreed between shipowner and agent, not set by port authorities
sources.recommended_acquisition_method: Use FONASBA framework to separate statutory disbursements from agency service fees in the data model
